title: Transfer from uniform affine étale torsion dimension to the topological-coefficient weak Serre hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with the discrete topology on $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology on the other rings [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The associated condensed ring is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$ on profinite sets. Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention], and ordinary internal module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume that for every affine étale morphism $v:V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and every integer $q>d$, one has $H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$ [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. Torsion here is local torsion, without a common annihilator.

Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal P_X$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$ containing zero and every finite constant scalar-model constructible module [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that if $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ is exact and $M',M''$ belong to the class, so does $M$. Then for every $M\in\mathcal P_X$ and every integer $q>d+2$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M[0])\bigr)=0.$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is the actual right derived functor of global sections of internal $\Lambda_X$-modules to abelian groups. No completion of modules or coefficients is made. No Noetherianity, finite-type structure map to a field, characteristic restriction, or invertibility of $\ell$ is assumed. Empty $X$, $d=0$, and the zero coefficient ring are included.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), first paragraph. Agent-formulated coefficient transfer obligation, separated from affine torsion geometry. Exact source WANTED. Compare Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Constructible sheaves on schemes, Section 8, condition (8.1) and Lemma 8.6, only for motivation: those results do not assert this weak-Serre hull statement with all-continuous norm-topological algebraic-closure coefficients.

proof.text: Let P be the weak Serre coproduct hull and B the property that H^r(RΓ(X,N[0])) vanishes for every r>d+2. Put Q=P∩B. Every constructible generator is in Q: realize it as its single complex, apply the finite-complex heart bound at the identity pro-etale object, and transport along upperStarId.

The long exact sequence of ordinary derived module sections makes B extension closed. It contains zero and is replete. Finite sums are extensions, and any small coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite partial sums. Apply the proved filtered continuity/ind-vanishing theorem in each r>d+2. Intersecting with P gives these closure properties for Q.

For a map f between Q objects, the bounded-kernel theorem applies because its sources are in P and both input bounds are part of Q. It gives B(kernel f); kernel closure of P gives Q(kernel f). For the cokernel, first use 0→ker(f)→M→coim(f)→0: the degree-r long exact sequence and the kernel bound in degree r+1 give B(coim(f)). Then use 0→coim(f)→N→coker(f)→0 to obtain B(coker(f)). Transport through arbitrary universal kernels and cokernels. This proves the actual cokernel step without a new obligation.

Now Q is a replete weak Serre coproduct class containing every constructible generator. Apply the defining minimality of P to hM. Its B component in degree q is the required conclusion. The finite discrete specialization stays proved by its direct etale-origin argument.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (2), first paragraph. X3 replaces the refuted arbitrary-affine filtered-heart approximation with weak Serre induction on P intersected with the cohomologically bounded objects. The complete Lean assembly uses one new kernel step; cokernel closure follows by two long exact sequences. This is a decomposition, with one new unresolved kernel obligation, not an unconditional proof.
